# Data Description: figure captions (generated by scripts/data_description.py)

**Figure 1. Participants in each wave.** The experiment ran 21 speed-dating events ("waves") between October 2002
and April 2004, with 551 participants: 274 women and 277 men. Waves ranged
from 10 to 44 participants; each person met every participant of the
opposite sex in their wave, so the number of dates ranged from 5 to 22 (median
16 per participant).

**Figure 2. Yes and match rates in each wave.** Across all 8,368 dating decisions, participants said yes
42.0% of the time, from 33.5% (wave 3) to 55.5% (wave 1). A
match, where both people said yes, happened in 16.5% of the 4,184 pairs, from
8.3% (wave 18) to 31.0% (wave 1). In wave 12 each person could say
yes to at most half of their dates.

**Figure 3. Who took part.** Participants' median age was 26 (range 18 to 55;
8 did not give an age). The most common reason for coming was "seemed like a fun night out"
(228 participants); 22 said they were looking for a serious
relationship.

Source: Columbia speed-dating experiment (Fisman, Iyengar, Kamenica and Simonson), Kaggle release. Counts leave out
10 scorecards with no partner id: in wave 5, ten men each rated a woman who has no record in the release (no
decision is missing anywhere). Tables: results/data_description_by_wave.csv and
results/data_description_goals.csv.
